title: Open Workout Schema v0: program
description: What a workout or multi-week program prescribes: weeks, then days, then slots. A single workout has one week with one day. A prescription, never performed work: loads are rules, not weights. Draft; may change until v1.

ows_version.description: The Open Workout Schema version the document was written to, as MAJOR.MINOR (SPEC.md, section 8).

schedule.description: How the days fall across a week, in words.

progression.description: How the targets change over time, in words.

weeks.description: The weeks of one cycle, repeating.

key.description: Stable within a version; what a link to this day names.

setGroup.description: A run of identical sets. Reps or a duration, not both.

amrap.description: As many reps as possible, reps_min at least.

percent.description: On a slot whose load is percent_training_max with no value: this group's own percentage of the training max, so a lift done as a ramp of sets at different weights is one slot. Then every group of the slot has one. Never on a stage.

loadPrescription.description: Where the load comes from. rpe takes a value; last and choice take none. percent_training_max takes a value, or none when every set group has its own percent, and may name the lift whose training max it works from in of. percent_of_slot takes a value and a day, and may name an exercise in of.

type.description: last: the load used last time on this slot, moved by the slot's progression rule. choice: the person's own pick. percent_of_slot: value percent of the current target of another slot, rounded down: the first slot on day whose exercise is of, or this slot's own exercise (Texas Method's volume day at 90% of the intensity day). It follows that slot, so it carries no progression rule; chains are allowed, cycles aren't. While the slot it reads has no weight yet, it waits on that slot's starting number.

day.description: percent_of_slot only: the key of the day whose slot it reads.

of.description: percent_training_max: the lift whose training max this slot works from, when it isn't the slot's own exercise (a front squat at a percentage of the back squat's training max). It reads that lift's training max as moved by that lift's own slots; a slot with of carries no progression rule. percent_of_slot: the exercise of the slot it reads, when it isn't this slot's own.

unit.description: % only on a linear rule's increment: that percentage of the load or training max it adds to, rounded to a step a bar can make, and at least one step (Madcow's 2.5% a week).

failureRule.description: After this many sessions in a row short of the slot's sets at one load, take drop_percent off and build back up. A session with reps unknown is neither short nor done.

stage_after_drops.description: linear with stages only, and required there: the drop that makes this many at one set scheme also moves on to the next scheme (StrongLifts: 5x5, then 3x5, then 3x3).

progressionRule.description: How the next session's load follows from the last one, on a slot whose load is last. A target is worked out when read and never changes the program or a past workout. Short means a set below its reps_min, or fewer sets than the slot asks for: the load stays, and on_fail decides when it drops. Missing data holds: a session with reps unknown on a set the rule reads, none missing and none logged short, is neither done nor short, so the load, stage and training max stay and a run of misses neither grows nor ends. linear: done (success) adds increment. A linear rule may carry stages: its on_fail drops as usual, and the drop that makes stage_after_drops drops at one set scheme also moves on to the next scheme (the last one stays), replayed in order like stages, each session read against the scheme it was suggested at; success is then all_sets. Where a rule reads an AMRAP set (increment_table, or linear with success amrap), it reads amrap_set when given, else the slot's last AMRAP set. double: every set at its reps_max adds increment; otherwise add reps at the same load. increment_table: the slot's AMRAP set picks the highest band whose reps_min it reached and adds that band's increment; below every band, the load stays. With success total_reps, a session is short when its sets add up to less than reps, which on_fail counts. stages: the slot's sets are the first stage and stages lists the ones after it; every set done adds increment at the same stage, a short session moves to the next stage at the same load, and a short session on the last stage starts again at the first stage from restart. The current stage follows from replaying the program's sessions in order, each read against the stage it was suggested at. Sessions of an exercise count for a slot only when logged on a day whose slot for that exercise has the same load and rule. variations, on a slot whose load is choice: moves the exercise, not the weight. ladder lists exercises easiest first, the slot's own among them; the step to do is the one logged last time (any step counts as the slot), or the next one when every planned set of it reached reps (rep sets) or hold_s seconds (timed sets). Unknown reps or times never count as reached. Every step of a ladder is measured the way the slot's sets are. linear and increment_table on a slot whose load is percent_training_max move the lift's training max instead of a load: start from the person's training max, then, oldest first, every session logged on a training-max slot of that lift with a rule adds what the rule adds when met, and counts a miss when short (on_fail takes its drop off the training max). Sessions on slots without a rule, or on no known day, leave it alone. Every percentage slot of the lift works from the result.

ladder.description: variations only: Open Exercise IDs, easiest first, each once, including the slot's own exercise.

hold_s.description: variations on timed sets: the hold every set must reach to move on.

increment.description: linear, double and stages: what a successful session adds.

stages.description: stages, or linear with on_fail.stage_after_drops: the set schemes after the slot's own sets, in order. Sets with reps.

restart.description: stages only, and required there: the load to start the first stage again from, after a short session on the last stage. The base load, less drop_percent, plus add, rounded down. Give drop_percent, add or both.

from.description: last: the load of the short session. first_stage_success: the last load every set of the first stage was done at (last when there is none).

success.description: linear: all_sets (the default): every set reached its reps_min. total_reps: the planned sets' reps add up to at least reps, and short means they don't, so a set that went further makes up for one short of its reps_min (5, 4, 6 reaches 15). increment_table may also take total_reps with reps: short then means under the total, and a session that reaches it adds the band its AMRAP set reached. amrap: the slot's AMRAP set reached at least reps. stages: all_sets (the default), or total_reps, where every set of the stage is there and their reps add up to at least the stage's reps_min, so a set that went further makes up for a short one.

reps.description: The threshold for success total_reps or amrap, or, on variations, the reps every set must reach to move on.

amrap_set.description: increment_table, or linear with success amrap: which of the slot's planned sets, counting from 1, the rule reads, when it isn't the last AMRAP set. It must be an AMRAP set.
